subject: Acme integration: request/response schema questions (chat vs completions, streaming)

Subject: Acme integration: request/response schema questions (post-call recap)

Hi Alex / Sana —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about the search+chat flow you want to ship. Quick recap and the open items we promised to follow up on: 

1) Request/response shape: you mentioned wanting structured tool-calling for product lookup and a JSON response envelope for downstream services. We flagged two options: chat-style messages (role/content arrays) vs completions-style prompts + structured output.

2) Tokenization and limits: you asked about how tokens are counted for combined prompt + schema, and practical guidance on max_tokens and stop sequences for structured output.

3) Streaming semantics: you want to stream partial results into your UI but preserve tool-call signals (i.e., when the model requests a product API call).

4) Embeddings/reranker: clarification on whether to embed the full doc or chunk+aggregate, and how to combine reranker scores with generation.

Next steps we propose:
- Dev (cc'd) to provide an SDK/technical note with examples for chat vs completions mapping, serialization, and streaming semantics.
- Share a small sample payload from your side (if possible) for us to sanity-check token counts and recommend max_tokens.
- Schedule a 30–45 min technical deep-dive next week (Dev + Rishi + your engineers).

Attachments: I dropped a short RFC with candidate response-envelope options (rfc-schema-v1.pdf) and a sample payload we discussed (acme_sample_payload.json).

If you can send the sample payload and preferred times, we’ll take it from there.

Thanks —

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. A few clarifications from our side before the engineering sync: 

- For structured output we prefer a top-level JSON envelope so our downstream can validate fields. Example: {"response": {"text": ..., "tools": [...]}}. Is that easier to enforce with chat or completions?

- Tokenization: our payloads sometimes include long product descriptions (up to ~1,800 tokens). We want guidance on whether to chunk at indexing time or at generation time, and the tradeoffs.

- Streaming + tool calls: we need tool-call events to be delivered reliably (even when streaming partial text). For example, if the model decides to call the product API mid-stream, we need a deterministic marker so our UI can pause text rendering and execute the call.

I attached a sample request payload (acme_sample_payload.json) with an example product doc and a couple of user queries.

Best —
Alex

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme integration: request/response schema questions (technical notes)

Hey all — quick technical notes based on the sample payload and questions. I pulled the details into bullets to keep it actionable.

1) Chat vs completions for structured envelope
- Both can work. Chat-style lets you preserve role metadata (system/user/assistant) which maps nicely to tool-calling APIs (assistant -> tool). Completions-style (single prompt) can be simpler for enforcing a JSON-only response via a strict instruction and stop tokens.
- Recommendation: use chat API when you need turn-level metadata and tool-calls; use completions-style with a strict response schema when you want a single JSON blob back and simpler token accounting.

2) Tokenization and max_tokens guidance
- Token accounting includes system+history+prompt+expected completion. For structured outputs, the schema increases token usage because you must serialize field names.
- With ~1,800 token product docs, two options: (a) chunk at indexing time and use a reranker to surface top-K chunks for generation (recommended), or (b) include condensed metadata in prompt and fetch full doc post-tool-call.
- For safety pick max_tokens ~512 for generative completion of the envelope and rely on tool-calls to retrieve full payloads. If you expect longer narrative fields, bump to 1,024 but monitor latency/cost.

3) Stop sequences and enforcing JSON
- Use explicit stop tokens that are unlikely to appear in content (e.g., "\n<<END_JSON>>"). For chat, you can also instruct the model to emit a single JSON object and then close the message. We provide a small SDK helper that validates and retries if parsing fails.

4) Streaming semantics + tool-calls
- Our streaming protocol emits incremental deltas for text plus structured events for tool-calls. The event sequence is deterministic: partial_text chunks, then a TOOL_CALL_START event with tool name + arguments, then TOOL_CALL_END, then resumed text.

- On the client, treat TOOL_CALL_START as a signal to pause text rendering and call your API. We also support an optional buffering mode where tool-call events are queued until the stream completes.

5) Embeddings & reranker
- Chunking at indexing time (e.g., 512–1,024 token chunks with overlap) + a semantic reranker gives best precision/recall. For long docs, aggregate chunk-level scores to rank documents, then pass top-ranked chunks into the generation context.
- For reranker vs embedding distance thresholds, we can share tuned defaults based on your dataset size in the technical deep-dive.

6) SDK & auth notes
- SDK supports both API-key and mTLS/KMS-based auth for Private deployments. We will provide example code for streaming + tool-calls in Node + Python.

Next steps: I can draft a short example mapping (chat message array -> completion JSON) and sample Node stream handler. If that works, propose a 45-min deep-dive Tuesday or Wednesday next week.
